Hi John — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) to meet AcmeHealth requirements for PHI processing and potential air-gapped deployment.
- Key customer asks: private control plane options, egress/ingress networking, KMS/HSM integration, SOC2 evidence, and proof-of-concept (PoC) plan for an air-gap test.

What we heard as blockers:
- Tight outbound rules in Acme network (no direct internet egress for inference nodes).
- Need for clear control-plane options (managed vs customer-controlled).
- Procurement wants SOC2 evidence and a list of ports/URLs for whitelist.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will send a short tech note with the control-plane options, high-level network requirements, and suggested port/URL allowlist — actionable for your infra team. (see attached network-diagram.pdf)
2) We’ll provide SOC2 artifacts and a stubbed evidence bundle for procurement to review (Aditya will attach the evidence zip).
3) Define a 2-week PoC: smoke tests for connectivity, on-prem deployment checklist, and an air-gap feasibility runbook if needed.

Can you confirm the timeline your infra team prefers for the PoC (week of 9/7 or 9/14)? Also looping in your infra contact if you want them on the thread.

Thanks — we’ll aim to keep the initial PoC low-friction (no production data until we have an agreed isolation design).

John / Infra team — thanks for the questions. Below is a concise technical response you can pass to procurement and security. I’ll also attach a diagram and our SOC2 evidence bundle for procurement review.

Short answers up front:
- Control plane: Redwood supports two primary deployment models for Private: 
  * Managed private control plane (hosted by Redwood but deployed into the customer VPC with no public internet egress required; control plane communicates over customer-provided endpoints).
  * Customer-managed control plane (full on-prem or VPC-deployed control plane that we handoff; no outbound calls to Redwood).
  Both options are supported; the customer-managed control plane is the recommended option for strictly air-gapped environments.

- Telemetry / phone-home: optional. We can disable outbound telemetry for air-gapped PoCs. When enabled (default managed path), telemetry is over TLS to configured endpoints; we can provide hashes and cert fingerprints for allowlisting.

- KMS/HSM: we support integration with customer KMS providers (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS) for envelope keys and can support HSM-backed keymaterial via standard KMIP or cloud-native APIs.

Network allowlist (minimum):
- Ports: 443 (TLS outbound for managed-control-plane option), 22 (SSH only for admin-engaged test windows), 2379 (etcd cluster comms if using our managed control plane in VPC), 10250 (kubelet) — note: these depend on deployment topology.
- FQDNs/IPs: For managed-control-plane option, we will provide an explicit list of FQDNs and IP ranges (per-region) prior to PoC. For customer-managed control plane / on-prem there are no egress requirements.

Suggested PoC test plan (2 weeks):
Week 1:
- Day 0–2: network validation — verify port/FQDN allowlist against a staging cluster using a minimal networking test harness.
- Day 3–5: deployment smoke tests — deploy a single inference worker, run 1k token generation tests, validate KMS integration with test keys.
Week 2:
- Day 6–9: air-gap runbook validation (if chosen) — simulate no external connectivity and validate inference on private images & local model cache.
- Day 10: review and next steps (production readiness checklist).

Attachments: redwood-private-arch.png (deployment variants), SOC2-evidence.zip (procurement bundle).

Next items from Redwood:
- We’ll create a 1-page hyperscaler vs Redwood private comparison (bulleted) and share by EOD today for procurement.
- Vanessa/Aditya: can we get your preferred PoC kickoff week confirmed? We propose w/c 2026-09-14 to align with Acme availability.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
